messages.subject: cable lengh
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Is there a function for calculating the cable length (skeleton distance) between two given nodes on a neuron ?

Thanks!
Arthur
messages.body_snippet:
Hi,

Is there a function for calculating the cable length (skeleton distance) between two given nodes on a neuron ?

Thanks!
Arthur

messages.subject: Re: cable lengh
messages.body_plain:
Dear Arthur,

Thanks for your message. For this kind of work the ngraph representation of neurons is pretty useful. There is an article on the documentation site <https://jefferis.github.io/nat/index.html> which gives an overview and worked examples

> Is there a function for calculating the cable length (skeleton distance) between two given nodes on a neuron ?

For your specific question, see this section of the article:

  https://jefferis.github.io/nat/articles/neurons-as-graph.html#walking-along-ngraph-objects

and in brief if you have a neuron, n

n=Cell07PNs[[1]]
ng=as.ngraph(n, weights=TRUE)
igraph::distances(ng, v=180, to=1)

note that in this case node indices (i.e. values between 1 and N, the number of nodes in the neuron) are being used.

You can also use the CATMAID id of the vertex (arbitrary integer). In that case you need to quote the ids (because they are used as the names of the nodes in the ngraph representation).

dl4=read.neurons.catmaid('glomerulus DL4 right')
ng=as.ngraph(dl4[[1]], weights=TRUE)
igraph::distances(ng, v=1, to=20)
igraph::distances(ng, v='7737299', to='44767283')

The whole article I mention above is worth a read and you can also look at this section of the function reference

https://jefferis.github.io/nat/reference/index.html#section-neurons-as-graphs-

Best wishes,

Greg.

messages.subject: Re: [nat-user] one against all error
messages.body_plain:
There is nothing to stop you from doing this although I confess it would still be slightly involved. The main difficulty would be to compute the bridging registration between the FlyCircuit 1.1 template brain and the one that we used to register all of the first round of data (a template that we synthesised from raw FlyCircuit image data that we call FCWB). We have a paper in progress describing much of our toolchain for which this would be a good addition, so we will try to do it by the end of the summer. All the best, Greg.

Sent from my iPhone

I see that using NBLAST on-the-fly, you are able to compare a FlyCircuit clone against all FlyLight Gal4 lines with NBLAST. Is it possible to similarly compare an uploaded tracing (or something like a segment of a FlyCircuit neuron) against the Gal4 lines? Is this feature also available using nblast directly in R? In trying to look into this, I came across the following link which is supposed to contain the dotprops data for the GMR Gal4 lines. However, the link appears to be broken.
http://flybrain.mrc-lmb.cam.ac.uk/si/nblast/www/nblast_desktop/

Apologies if there is some documentation that I'm missing.
Thanks for your help
Isabel

messages.subject: Re: stumbling to implement the nat package
messages.subject_clean: stumbling to implement the nat package
messages.body_plain:
Dear Andy,

Thanks for your interest in nat. I hope it will be useful to you.

I have only implemented reading of ascii format Amira surface objects in the current version of nat. You would therefore need to go back to Amira and resave your surface objects in the Amira HyperSurface ASCII format.

If this is possible it would be the simplest. I do however have preliminary support for the binary surface format already implemented but not sufficiently complete that I wanted to release. I could nevertheless make this available for testing if it would be helpful.

Best wishes,

Greg.

PS I have taking the liberty of ccing the nat-user google group in case this answer might be useful to others.

Sent from my iPhone
